newsitem.title: USA: Ohio DOT plans $220 mln of bonds in fiscal 1998.
newsitem.headline: Ohio DOT plans $220 mln of bonds in fiscal 1998.

text.p: Ohio Department of Transportation plans to issue $220 million of bonds in fiscal 1998 for $950 million of construction projects, the department said Friday.

Cost cutting and new revenues will allow the department to issue $220 million of bonds in fiscal years 1999 and 2000 as well, but the uncertain long term outlook prevents Ohio from committing to major new highway projects beyond a four-year forecast, the department said in an annual report.

"Presently, ODOT is depending on additional bond sales and internal operating cost savings to maintain its near-record construction program," the report states. "However, within three years the department will not be able to sustain additional bond sales and its operating costs will begin to rise again."
The fiscal 1999 bonds will finance major new construction, while the fiscal 2000 bonds, if necessary, would finance reconstruction on multi-lane roads, the department said.
The department also plans to begin leasing its right of way for cellular phone towers and may increase fees on overweight trucks to generate new revenue, the report stated.

Maintenance costs for the aging state transportation system have continued to rise as greater motor vehicle fuel efficiency has slowed the rate of increase in gasoline tax receipts to fund repairs, the department reported.
